open_points.subject: A01 rule 4 duplicate-submission behavior
open_points.text: `canonical_values` owns “A01 rules 1 and 4” but knows only `models`, `data_provider`, and “Must not own where a value is stored”; A01 rule 4 requires returning an existing stored record, preserving its first author and time, recording nothing, and not changing which version is current.
open_points.question: Which module owns and atomically enforces the stored-record behavior of an equal submission, as distinct from computing content identity?
options: `canonical_values` owns only identity/equality; each record-owning module enforces duplicate-submission semantics through `store`
`store` provides one generic atomic insert-or-return-existing operation that enforces A01 rule 4
Expand `canonical_values` so it may access stored records
open_points.default_guess: Limit `canonical_values` to identity computation and make each record-owning module enforce A01 rule 4 through an atomic store capability.

open_points.subject: operation-port validation during run advancement
open_points.text: “a receiving element of either kind refused a misfit input (A13 rule 3) — is built and written by `runs`”, but `runs` knows `functions`, `flows` and `effects`, not `bindings`; a FlowNode contains only `binding_id`, while the operation port schemas are owned by `bindings`.
open_points.question: How does `runs` obtain an operation node's input-port definitions to validate an input before `effects` is called?
options: Move operation-input validation and its NodeExecution to `effects`
open_points.default_guess: Add `bindings` to `runs` dependencies and read the accepted binding through `bindings.read_binding`.

open_points.subject: minted record identities
open_points.text: A01 rule 2 says `trial_execution_id`, `binding_id`, `run_id`, `approval_id` and `grant_id` “are minted at random by the kernel; one that already exists is minted again”, but State 3 assigns neither random generation nor the collision-check-and-remint operation to a module.
open_points.question: Which module owns random ID generation and guarantees collision detection and reminting atomically?
options: `store` mints every random record ID inside the creating transaction
Each record-owning module generates candidates and asks `store` to reject collisions
A separate lower-level identity/randomness module owns minting
open_points.default_guess: Have `store` mint and collision-check these IDs inside the transaction that creates each record.

open_points.subject: `models` validation responsibility
open_points.text: `models` owns “plain typed data, with their closed status and class enumerations. No behaviour”, “Must not own Validation”, yet its depth assessment names “type validity of the kernel's shared vocabulary” as its hidden mechanism.
open_points.question: Does `models` enforce runtime construction/type validity, or does it only declare data shapes and enumerations while other modules validate them?
options: `models` only declares passive types and enumerations; callers own all validation
`models` constructors enforce structural type validity but not domain rules
open_points.default_guess: Treat `models` as passive declarations, allowing only language-level type construction checks and leaving runtime/domain validation to the owning modules.
